rules.content: Standing rule for dev servers, test services and local tools: never use common ports such as 8080, 8000, 5000 or 3000. Pick a random port above 3000, for example 3076, 6759 or 43510.
Standing rule for Python: create environments with uv (uv venv --python 3.12, then uv pip install -r requirements.txt). Never python3 -m venv and never pip install into the system interpreter.
No Co-Authored-By trailer and no 'Generated with Claude Code', robot emoji or Anthropic attribution anywhere: commits, PR and MR descriptions, issues, code comments and docs. The code is the user's.
Commit messages are a single title line. No body, no bullet list underneath.
Never git add -A, git add . or git commit -a. Stage files by explicit path, then check git diff --cached --name-only before committing; node_modules, build output and screenshots never go in.
User interfaces carry no descriptive or explanatory sentences: no page intros, no chart captions, no empty-state advice. Labels and values only, in every project.
Every interface defaults to a light theme: white or light grey background, dark text. Dark mode exists only as an opt-in toggle. 3D scenes default to daylight and bright lighting.
PR and MR descriptions contain exactly one line, 'Closes #N' (or 'Closes #N. Closes #M.'), so the work item is linked and closed on merge. Never leave the description empty.
Throwaway js, python or shell scripts (debugging, reproductions, launch helpers) never go into a repository. They live in the scratchpad or /tmp.
Keys and tokens are never written into a file that gets committed. Code reads them from ~/.config/<service>/key or an environment variable, and they never appear in logs or command lines.
No Docker on the Mac: container builds and container tests run on the Linux cluster nodes or the dell VMs, never locally.

not_rules.content: PR and MR descriptions are left completely empty.
Prefers tabs over spaces in Makefiles, mildly.
Athanor's frontend uses Tailwind and shadcn components only, no hand-written CSS.
CortexDB keeps pkg/cortexdb flat with topic-prefixed files instead of sub-packages.
For this session only: the terminal recording uses a dark theme to match the video.
